task: Fix test-suite log pollution in ~/.codemie/logs caused by an unset CODEMIE_HOME override during tests, and improve hook error visibility/logging clarity in user environments.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches 4-5 distinct components across 4 layers (test setup, Logger singleton, HookExecutor, hook.ts CLI entry, hooks-loader.ts) — baseline L for 'shared utilities involved', then bumped by two distinct red flags to XXL.

The 'improve hook error visibility/logging clarity' half of the task has no defined acceptance criteria (what counts as sufficiently visible, whether a new env var or default-behavior change is expected); technical-analysis.md explicitly flags this as an open design decision for spec/plan.

Task description names a specific failure mode (test-log pollution via unset CODEMIE_HOME) and targets the hook error-path behavior directly, but zero existing tests cover HookExecutor, hook.ts, hooks-loader.ts, prompt-executor.ts, matcher.ts, or decision.ts — any change here ships without a regression safety net on exactly the defensive pattern being modified.

technical-analysis.md's own 'Architecture and Layers Affected' section enumerates 4 layers touched: CLI (hook.ts), Core/Engine (executor.ts, prompt-executor.ts, decision.ts, matcher.ts), Plugin (hooks-loader.ts, Claude plugin hook transformer lookup), and Utils (logger.ts, errors.ts, proxy-logger.ts).

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L to XL: touches core shared utilities (Logger singleton, 228 callers across the codebase)

Component Scope bumped from XL to XXL: affects multiple workflows/agents (hook.ts's `codemie hook` command is the single shared entry point invoked by every agent plugin's hook script — Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, Kimi)
Requirements Clarity bumped from L to XL: vague acceptance criteria — 'improve hook error visibility/logging clarity' names no concrete success criteria

Technical Risk bumped from L to XL: task names a specific error-path failure mode (test-log pollution) with no existing test template covering this defensive/error-path pattern anywhere in the untested hooks subsystem
